### Observed differences

- A03 occurred in every earlier trace (about 2 times per trace, repeated in about 44 in 100 traces, with its outgoing transitions split roughly equally between A05 and A04); in the later window it does not occur at all. [OCC003, DIR003, POS003, REL011]
- A02 and A01 were absent earlier; in the later window each occurs once in every trace — A02 at the very start (median position about 0) and A01 around two-thirds into the trace (median position about 0.75). [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002]
- Earlier, A06 always led back to A03, forming a loop A03 → A04 → A06 → A03 that ran at least once in about 44 in 100 traces; A04 and A06 never appeared without A03. [DIR004, REL010, REL012, LAG001, LAG003]
- In the later window the loop runs without A03: A02 sends about 51 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A04 and about 48 in 100 to A01, while A06 now leads to A01 (about 53 in 100) or back to A04 (about 46 in 100); A01 in turn leads to A05 in about 995 of 1000 transitions. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004]
- A04 and A06 now appear in about 50 in 100 traces, up from about 44 in 100, and the distance between consecutive A04 (or A06) occurrences shortened from about 3 steps to about 2 steps, with some 4-step repeats — consistent with the loop containing one activity fewer. [POS004, POS005, LAG001, LAG005]
- Later-window ordering: A02 precedes A01 in about 98 in 100 traces, A01 precedes A05 in all traces, and in about 28 in 100 traces A04 (or A06) precedes A01 while in about 22 in 100 they interleave or repeat. [REL001, REL003, REL004, REL007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reorganisation around the A04–A06 loop: A03 — previously the entry point, loop hub and exit route to A05 — no longer occurs, A02 now starts every trace, and A01 is inserted between the loop and A05. In the later window, traces begin with A02, which either starts the loop at A04 or goes directly to A01; the loop repeats via A06 → A04 and exits via A06 → A01, after which A01 leads to A05. The signs are direct and mutually consistent: participation in A01 and A02 rose from none to all 200 traces while A03 fell from all 200 to none; the successor profiles of A02, A06 and A01 show exactly this rewiring; the relation indicators show the A02 → A01 → A05 sequence; and the shortening of the A04/A06 repeat distance from about 3 to about 2 steps matches A03 dropping out of the cycle. Screening flagged 29 control-flow items where about 0.17 would be expected without a change, so chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL001, REL004, REL011, LAG001, LAG005, screening]

The evidence cannot distinguish whether A03 was genuinely removed or its role was relabelled into A02 and A01, nor whether the new entry point and the new exit step were one coordinated rewiring or two separate adjustments; position and lag indicators use event order, so no conclusion about clock-time timing follows. [OCC003, POS001, POS002, LAG001]

Other differences:

- Two rare transitions appear only in the later window — A02 directly to A05 and A01 back to A02 — each about 5 in 1000 of the observed outgoing transitions of its source (roughly 1 case in 200). [DIR001, DIR002]
- The distance from A04 to A05, previously a uniform 3 steps, is now about 3 steps in roughly half of the observed pairs and 5 steps in about 15 in 100, reflecting traces that repeat the loop before reaching A05. [LAG002]
